note: Quiet Sunday: only a handful of AI sends, one of them fully sponsored.

top.title: Morgan Stanley's rollout playbook: race the AI against an expert, then keep grading it
top.summary: Before launch, Morgan Stanley gave its adviser assistant and a subject expert 25 real questions and an hour each, then built a 500-question regression suite it reruns after every change and grades a daily sample of live answers against a rubric. Advisers have since made nearly 50,000 attempts at building their own agents, many of them used once and abandoned.
top.why: This is a ready-made quality gate for PMM workflows (fixed test set, rerun on every change, daily spot checks), and the abandoned-agent number is a warning for any self-serve agent building program you run.

top.title: Study of 260 multi-agent setups finds more agents often add overhead, not quality
top.summary: A sponsored deep dive on shared human-agent workspaces cites a Nature Machine Intelligence study where adding agents did not reliably improve results, and argues agents need shared context, an owner, scoped permissions and a record of state. It recommends letting agents prepare work freely but requiring human approval before anything is sent outside, changed in a system of record, or paid for.
top.why: The 'preparation vs. commitment' line is a clean rule for where to put human review in PMM workflows, and the coordination argument supports Camunda's story that agents need orchestration, not just more agents.

top.title: 44% of marketers run AI agents with customers, but only 19% can report results
top.summary: An Invoca survey of 451 US marketers found 44% already have AI agents talking to customers, yet only 19% can send chat outcomes back to ad platforms and 26% can tie a chat to the ad that started it. Invoca sells call tracking, so it has a stake in the finding.
top.why: A concrete data point that agent deployment is outrunning measurement, useful both for framing AI impact reporting and as an orchestration-and-visibility proof point in Camunda messaging.

try_this.title: Run a 25-question expert race on one PMM workflow
try_this.how: Pick 25 real questions your team fields (positioning, competitor claims, product facts), give your AI workflow and a subject expert an hour each, and grade both on accuracy and completeness. Save the set as a regression test and rerun it whenever you change the prompt or skill.

measurement.title: Morgan Stanley reports 1.4 million developer hours saved, with no dollar figure
measurement.summary: The bank says its DevGen.AI tool and related use cases have saved more than 1.4 million hours across 950+ onboarded use cases, and 98% of adviser teams adopted its assistant. It has not published accuracy scores or total AI spend.
measurement.why: A reminder that hours-saved claims land better with a stated method and cost side, which is worth building into your own time-saved reporting.

landscape.title: Forrester expects brands to put human-made content back at the top in 2027
landscape.summary: Forrester predicts half of brands will prioritize human-made content next year as buyers look for proof of real expertise, and reports only 18% of US online adults trust information from AI.
landscape.why: Helps decide which PMM outputs AI should draft versus which need visible human expertise, especially thought leadership aimed at technical buyers.

landscape.title: The Ringer drops its ChatGPT podcast sponsorship after listener pushback
landscape.summary: The Ringer ended ChatGPT segments on its biggest shows because its audience disliked them, even as OpenAI spent about $11.2 million on podcast ads over three months.
